cohort: 3038 women who gave birth in 2008 and 3001 women who gave birth in 2014 at the university maternity unit in Caen, France
finding: There was a significant increase in all types of Cesarean sections among women born abroad compared to those born in France, especially in the subgroup of women born in sub-Saharan Africa.
mod_finding: Women born in sub-Saharan Africa had a significant decrease in spontaneous labors and a significant increase in emergency cesarean sections before and during labor compared to non-migrants.
